terms.comment: Both forms are classical. The feminine sīmia is the commoner (Plautus, Cicero, Pliny) and is used of either sex; the masculine is Phaedrus’s and Martial’s (Lewis & Short), and the one this lexicon leads with.

evidence: Plaut. Mil. 2.2.7; Cic. Div. 1.76; Plin. NH 8.215 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The commoner classical form (Plautus, Cicero, Pliny), used of either sex; sīmius is Phaedrus’s and Martial’s (Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: simius / simia
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
